Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

UtilsR 0.6.14

  • pr_table() describes every component of a matrix or array column per row instead of silently showing only its first component.

  • pr_table() reads columns by position, preserving distinct contents when column names repeat or are empty.

  • pr_table() respects the direction of text P-value bounds, including Unicode comparisons and whitespace, and does not mark invalid numeric text as significant. Numeric P-values keep enough decimals below a cut-off and values below 0.001 print as <0.001.

  • pr_table() preserves integer64 digits and time-span components instead of formatting their underlying storage. Print helpers load the namespace supporting stored integer64, labelled and lubridate values when needed.

UtilsR 0.6.13

  • fmt_axisTile() works with panel sizes fixed through theme(panel.widths, panel.heights) (ggplot2 4.0). Fixing the size along the tiled axis stopped the plot with “Cannot create zero-length unit vector”, since ggplot2 counted the colour strip as a panel; the strip now keeps its tile_height / tile_width fraction of the fixed panel size. RegR’s plt_screens() needs it.

UtilsR 0.6.12

  • lv() prints each variable’s suggested get_flt() call on a light grey ground with black text, like inline code, where the console shows colour. Copied from the console it is plain text, and without colour (knitting, log files, capture.output()) it prints plain.

  • pr_spark() summarizes integer64 and other classed numeric columns as plain numbers. The mean of an integer64 column is itself an integer64, which formatC() wrote as its raw bits, a line of some 300 digits that pushed every other line’s missing share off the screen, and the sparkline came out flat.

  • lv()’s console report opens with a summary of the data set, as skimr’s Data Summary does: the number of rows and variables, the variables by type (4 factor, 3 character, 3 numeric), and those with missing or Unknown/Blank/N/A values. These had appeared only in the HTML table’s subtitle.

  • A numeric variable with more than ten values is listed by its distribution at lv()’s console, as skimr gives it: a sparkline, the range, median [Q1, Q3] and mean (SD). Counts of its first values (ages 0, 1, 2, …) said little about it. Numeric codes with up to ten values keep their frequency table.

  • At the console, lv() lists each variable in one block, set off by a blank line: a heading with its counts (Grade (factor) · 5 levels · special 4,271 (93.9%)), a frequency table of values with n, pct and cumulative cum shares of all rows, missing values last, and the suggested get_flt() call. Beyond 15 values the rest are summed in one (k others) row. Each variable had two headings (count and unique values) over a dplyr::count() tibble that hid missing values beyond its tenth row.

  • lv()’s variable summary gives each count of missing and of Unknown/Blank/N/A values with its share of the rows (4,271 (93.9%)), at the console in an aligned pr_table() rather than a tibble. In the HTML table those counts are shaded red and blue where there are any, as in the count table, a note names the shades and the type tints, and the suggested get_flt() call is left-aligned in monospace and shortened to one line (the console prints it whole); it had been centred and wrapped over up to four lines.

  • pr_table() no longer replaces the cells of a first column one to three characters wide with dots where the console has no Unicode: it cut every cell to the column width, and cli::ansi_strtrim() gives its ... ellipsis cut to a width narrower than itself even for text that fits ("A" became "."). Only cells too wide for the column are cut.

  • At the console, lv() gives one pr_spark() line per variable under “Variable distributions”: a sparkline, the mean and SD or the levels and the most frequent one, and the share missing. It replaces the summary table printed as a tibble, whose cells carried the table’s markdown (**Vars**, __Age (numeric, 91)__) and NA for each variable row.

  • lv(count = c(a, b)) gives one two-way table, as janitor’s adorn_totals() + adorn_percentages("row") + adorn_ns() lay it out: each cell shows the count and the row percentage (1,285 (64.8%)), a Total row the column counts and their shares of all rows, and a Total column the row counts. It replaces the long list, the wide table and the row-percentage table that two variables used to print; in the HTML table the second variable names its columns as a spanner. Columns are sorted as factor levels or values.

  • lv() writes counts with thousands separators and shares with one decimal throughout. The cross-tabulation list printed n, pct and n_pct, the same share twice with two decimals that dropped trailing zeros (1285 (28.25%) beside 655 (14.4%)); it now gives n and pct (28.2%) in an aligned console table. The wide table’s cells and the subtitles of both tables (n = 4549, 4549 observations) take separators too.

  • lv()‘s count table gives each shade one meaning and names those it uses in a note under the table. Shares of rare categories darken in one hue, light orange for 5-10%, orange for 1-5% and dark orange below 1%; labels of missing rows are light red and of Unknown/Blank/N/A values light blue, as in check_na(). Red had marked both missing rows and shares below 1%, yellow both special values and shares of 1-5%, green shares of 5-10%, all without a legend. Missing rows’ shares are no longer shaded as rare categories.

  • lv()’s suggested get_flt() filters print as plain lines, without print()’s [1] prefix, so they copy as code, and list the values of character, numeric, logical and date columns sorted as the count listing above them sorts them, rather than in the order they occur (c(66, 72, 70, ...) for ages). Factors keep their level order.

  • Outside interactive sessions, such as Rscript or an RStudio background job, lv() no longer prints its HTML tables, which arrived as HTML source (some 500 lines per table; lv() of a 93-column data frame wrote 3,903 lines instead of 1,087). A message says the tables were not shown.

  • lv(group = )’s table carries a caption naming the grouping and the number of rows, Variable summary by Sex (n = 4,549), as the default summary table names its data.

  • Knitted lv() reports no longer head each variable with a ** summary for x (class) ** message: the console listings it headed are left out of knitted documents, so each heading stood over nothing.

  • The missing rows of lv()’s summary tables give their share of the rows beside the count, 418 (9.2%) rather than 418, in the default and the grouped table.

  • lv() no longer prints Setting theme "Compact" on every call; the compact gtsummary theme it sets for its own tables is set quietly.

  • lv() selects columns through a caller’s vector of names or positions, lv(data, vars) or lv(vars), without tidyselect’s “Using an external vector in selections was deprecated” warning: such a vector, also inside c(), - or !, is wrapped in all_of(). Column names still take precedence over caller objects of the same name.

  • fmt_tag() no longer keeps the plots it tags inside each in-panel label. The label layer was built in fmt_tag()’s own frame, which its mapping and geom kept, so every tagged plot carried all the others: the first of four tagged 1e5-point plots held the data of all four, and a RegR::get_rcs_all() composite saved with saveRDS() took 11.9 MB instead of 9.5 MB. The labels draw as before.

  • A pr_tree() line still too wide for a narrow console, such as a data frame with an attribute tag, ends in an ellipsis; cli::tree() cut it off without one, leaving term, HR [ at 40 columns.

  • pr_tree() says what it left out: ... 25 more goes on with the names of the elements it skipped (... 25 more: e6, e7, e8, ...), and the footer names the argument that cut the lines (# ... 16 more lines (max_lines = 9)).

  • pr_tree() pads the names of siblings to a common width, up to 18 characters, so their descriptions start in one column, as str() and pr_kv() line them up.

  • pr_tree() names the attributes a closed node carries at the end of its line, such as [attr: model_info] on a result table or [attr: plot_size] on a plot, leaving out those its type keeps for itself (factor levels, a time zone, value labels, ggplot2’s S7 properties). Only the attributes of open nodes were shown, so these went unseen. attrs = FALSE drops them.

  • pr_tree() gives a factor’s number of levels, <fct 100, 3 levels>, as str() does.

  • pr_tree() takes as many values as the line could hold and ends a vector it cut with an ellipsis: at a width of 100, 1:100 read 1, 2, ..., 10, as if that were all.

  • pr_tree() opens the object it is given: a model fit lists its components, a data frame its columns and an S4 object its slots (as @name), where each printed a single line such as <lm>. Inside a list they stay closed, as before.

  • pr_tree() follows a data frame with its column names, as many as fit the line: <tibble 12 x 5> term, HR, lower, upper, p.

  • A list pr_tree() leaves closed, at max_depth or as an attribute, previews its names and the value of each single one: attr analysis <list 2> n = 1000, outcome = "DSS" read attr analysis <list 2>. An unnamed list keeps the ellipsis.

  • pr_tree() names the element type of a matrix or table (<int matrix 2 x 3>) and the arguments of a function (<fn(data, formula, ...)>, the first four), which read <matrix 2 x 3> and <fn>.

  • pr_tree() shows whole numbers as they are and decimals to three digits past their integer part: rounded to three significant digits, 123456L read 123000 and 1234.5678 read 1230.

  • pr_tree() names classed vectors as vctrs does, such as <drtn 2> for a difftime, <dbl+lbl 3> for a labelled vector and <int64>, where they read <dbl ...>; a POSIXlt time shows as <dttm> with its value instead of <POSIXlt>.

  • pr_tree() previews show the names of a named vector (train = 800, test = 200), the value labels of a labelled one (1 [Male]), factor levels without quotes, and formulas, calls and symbols as written (<formula> Surv(time, DSS) ~ Age + Sex), which read only <formula>. pr_kv() describes formulas the same way.

  • pr_tree() previews fill the line up to the console width and end in an ellipsis, where they stopped at 40 characters, or were cut off without one on a narrow console. Lengths and dimensions carry a thousands mark, <int 1,000,000> and <data.frame 12,345 x 7>, in pr_kv() too.

  • pr_tree() colours the parts of a line apart: the type and size stay grey, values take the console’s text colour with NA in red, and the names of elements that hold others are bold. The whole description, values included, used to be grey.

  • pr_tree() starts with the class chip only for a classed list, the case it is meant for; a plain list, a vector or a data frame no longer repeats its class (<list> <list 3> now reads <list 3>).

  • .cat_formula() no longer counts a missing outcome value as a level, so a binary outcome with NAs is announced as a Cox model, not a CRR one.

  • .cat_message() prints every element of a character vector, each on its own line; it showed only the first. A zero-length message prints nothing instead of failing with “subscript out of bounds”, and a missing one prints NA instead of failing with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”.

  • pr_box() prints nothing when there is nothing to frame, such as a list whose elements are all NULL, instead of failing with “a character vector argument expected”.

  • .cat_message(timestamp_format = NULL) or timestamp_format = "" leaves the timestamp out. An empty format used to fall back to R’s default date-time format, so the timestamp stayed, without its brackets.

  • pr_tree() stops describing nodes once it reaches max_lines and only counts the rest, so a large nested list prints its first lines at once: a 20 x 20 x 20 list took 2.5 s to print 200 lines, now 0.07 s. The printed lines are unchanged.

  • pr_kv() and pr_head() show numbers as print() does, to getOption("digits") significant digits: 1/3 read 0.333333333333333. pr_head() also shows a factor piece as its label and a date as a date, where it showed the factor code and the day count.

  • pr_table() shows a P value just under 0.05 or 0.01 with the decimals it needs, 0.0499* rather than 0.050*: rounded to three decimals it read as the cut-off, beside a 0.050 with no star.

  • pr_table() gains rownames: TRUE shows the row names as a first, unnamed column, such as the terms of a coefficient matrix turned data frame, which are otherwise not shown. It is off by default, since rbind() of a named list also leaves row names (cox.1, cox.2).

  • pr_table() cuts a first column too wide for the line with an ellipsis: long variable labels made the table overflow width, as the first and the P-value columns always show.

  • pr_note() starts a new line at each "\n", as pr_kv() does; the lines of a note were joined with a space.

  • pr_table() describes the cells of a list column as pr_tree() does, <dbl 2> 1.1, 2.2, where it printed the deparsed c(1.1, 2.2).

  • pr_spark() shows a column whose values all differ, such as a patient identifier, as <n> unique values instead of tabulating it: 1e5 identifiers took 0.1 s to draw a flat line of single counts.

  • PlotButterfly(), PlotButterfly2() and PlotRankCor() announce a saved plot with .cat_saved(), as the other plotting functions do: PlotRankCor: the plot has been saved to: <path> [7x5 in, new PDF], in place of Plot saved to <path>.

  • lv() prints its headings and facts at the console with pr_section() and pr_kv(), on stdout beside the tables they head (cross-tabulation, wide and row-percentage tables, grouped summary, Seurat summary and cell statistics), so capture.output() and Rscript logs keep them and suppressMessages() no longer strips them from the report. The banner above each variable, which the console listing already names, is left out there. Knitted reports keep the cli headers as before.

UtilsR 0.6.11

  • plt_cat() and plt_con() with split.by report the size of the split figure once again. Each panel’s own “plot laid out for” note was captured as printed output, which a .cat_message() no longer is since it became a cli message, so a figure of three panels showed four notes.

  • pr_tree() keeps gt tables, RegR pages and htmltools tag lists closed: they are lists underneath, and opening one listed some 20 internal fields, such as _data and _styles, in place of the result’s parts. R6 objects, such as mlr3 learners, show their class instead of <env>, in pr_tree() and pr_kv() alike.

  • .cat_formula() announces a model in one .cat_message() line, e.g. Cox model, unadjusted: Surv(time, DSS) ~ Sex, instead of a box and a rule, nine lines in all; suppressMessages() silences it.

  • .cat_message(wrap = FALSE) keeps every line whole, for a line meant to be copied, such as a save = list(...) call.

  • New .cat_saved() announces a written file as <subject>: <path> [<size>, new PDF], or replaced the existing PDF in red, as a .cat_message(); it moves here from RegR. PlotCircleLollipop(), PlotDumbbell(), PlotHeatmapJaccard(), PlotRank() and PlotScatter1() to PlotScatter3() use it for their filename, with the function name and the page size, instead of message("Plot saved to: ").

UtilsR 0.6.10

  • PlotRankCor() prints its per-group correlations as a pr_table() with the P values coloured by significance. The coefficient column is r for use_rank = FALSE, as in the subtitle; the printed lines called a Pearson coefficient rho.

  • pal_list() and console pal_show() head each palette with a pr_section() rule, "Set1 (9 colours, discrete)", instead of a === banner; so do the pal_show_*() wrappers.

  • check_system(show_warnings = TRUE) emits one acquisition warning when a memory backend fails, preserving its cause without a duplicate warning.

  • check_system() measures R heap bytes with lobstr or exact GC cell counts, removing the undeclared pryr dependency and rounded-MB fallback. Reports and warnings label binary memory units as GiB; existing _gb field names, thresholds and function arguments are retained.

  • check_system() avoids repeated Windows CIM startup when ps can query live memory. Only static OS and CPU metadata are cached; memory is refreshed on every call, with fresh CIM queries retained if the native backend fails.

  • check_system() obtains macOS memory through the optional ps backend, using available memory consistently instead of attempting Linux commands.

  • check_system() fills missing Windows text fields independently, preserving valid CIM memory and metadata. A CPU query failure no longer discards OS information, and CSV parsing preserves version strings.

  • check_system() handles unknown logical core counts while retaining known physical counts. On Linux, the optional ps backend distinguishes physical cores from hardware threads; without it the physical count is missing.

  • check_system() validates memory totals and available memory on every backend, preventing negative, non-finite or out-of-range usage. Missing Linux cache fields use a conservative free-memory fallback.

  • check_system() reports unavailable memory as scalar missing values when Windows queries return no results, while retaining the remaining diagnostics.

  • check_system() matches complete Linux memory fields, so the fallback for missing MemAvailable does not mistake SwapCached for Cached.

  • check_packages() reports library counts with pr_head(), pr_table() and pr_note(), highlighting the total and fitting long paths to the console. Table counts use comma thousands separators, matching the header. It returns the same data frame invisibly, retaining full paths and counts.

  • The print helpers write no colour codes when standard output shows no colour, as when Rscript x.R > log.txt runs in a terminal. pr_note() and .cat_step() show text that cli cannot parse, such as data with braces, as written instead of failing. Without colour (knitted documents, log files) class labels read <class>, badges [key: value], and pr_table() marks significance with stars, highlighted rows with > and missing text cells with <NA>. pr_spark() shows an empty-string level as "".

  • pr_table() gains n (20 rows by default, NULL for all) and width (the console width by default): it keeps the first and the P-value columns, adds the others while they fit, and counts the rows and names the columns left out in a grey footer. A column whose smallest non-zero value would round to zero gets enough decimals for two significant digits (0.0003 printed as 0.00).

  • pr_kv() and pr_box() wrap long values at the console width under the value column, indent the lines of values with newlines the same way, and show at most 20 items of a vector followed by its length. pr_note() wraps long notes with a # on every line, and .cat_message() wraps long lines under the message text. pr_head() cuts a line longer than the console with an ellipsis, and pr_section() a title too long for its rule, which cli::rule() had cut without one. pr_kv() describes object values by type and size, e.g. <data.frame 6 x 11> rather than <data.frame>.

  • pr_tree() previews the first values of atomic vectors (<chr 3> "Age", "Sex", "Stage"), marks a list left unopened at max_depth with an ellipsis, and gains max_lines (200 by default), past which a grey footer counts the rest.

  • pr_spark() gives few whole numbers one bar per value, so no empty bin falls between two values, and shows date and date-time columns as a histogram with their first and last dates instead of <Date>.

UtilsR 0.6.9

  • check_packages() collects counts before constructing its result, avoiding repeated data-frame copies while retaining library order and count semantics.

  • check_packages() warns about missing, inaccessible or unreadable libraries and continues counting the others. Failed counts and the total are NA, so incomplete results cannot be mistaken for an empty library or a full total.

  • check_packages(refresh = TRUE) reads installed-package counts from disk instead of cached metadata. The default keeps the existing cache behavior.

  • check_packages() replaces count_packages_in_libpaths() with the same per-library installed-package counts and total. The old name is removed.

  • The report of check_system() uses the print helpers: a class label with the time, one rule per group and the Chinese keys aligned by display width. It now goes to standard output, so suppressMessages() no longer hides it; wrap the call in capture.output() to keep only the returned list. check_size() with nothing selected says so in a grey note. check_na() heads its table with a class label giving the variable count (green when nothing is missing) and reports empty input in grey notes. In the console, lv() heads each variable’s count and level listings and its overall tables with grey rules instead of ---- and ** ** lines; its cli headers, which knitr shows as messages, stay as they were.

  • fct_cat(ref_idx = 0) is the same as ref_idx = NULL: nothing collapses, and another mode given alongside still runs. Only a single 0 means none; a 0 among indices is still out of range.

  • New print helpers for S3 print methods. pr_head() prints a class label on a solid background followed by a grey one-line summary. pr_kv() prints a key-value block, keys in grey and aligned by display width. pr_section() prints a grey rule led by a bold title. pr_note() prints a grey italic # ... line with cli inline markup, so {.run pkg::fun(x)} becomes a clickable link in consoles that support hyperlinks. pr_badge() returns two-part key-value badges (key on dark grey, value on a chosen colour) to combine on one line. pr_table() prints a data frame as an aligned plain-text table: columns aligned by display width, P-value columns coloured by significance (bold red below 0.001, red below 0.05) and chosen rows highlighted. pr_tree() prints the structure of a nested result list as a tree with short grey descriptions such as <tibble 12 x 7>, listing extra attributes as well. pr_box() frames key-value or plain lines in a rounded box with an optional header and footer in its border. pr_spark() prints one line per column: a sparkline of its distribution, a short summary and the missing share.

  • plt_dist() takes its plot settings as plt_alluvial()-style lists: label_args, flow_args, stratum_args, facet_args and legend_args. The standalone label, gap and curve_type arguments are removed; use label_args$style, stratum_args$gap and flow_args$curve_type. label_args also sets min_pct (leave small segments unlabelled), pct_accuracy, size, color, box, fill and alpha, and style = "count_percent_wrap" puts counts and percentages on separate lines.

  • plt_dist(type = "bar") labels default to one line, count (percent), in white boxes (previously count\n(percent) in boxes filled with the segment colour), and the y axis shows percentages. Bar and alluvial label counts use a comma as thousands separator.

  • plt_dist() bar facets count only the facet values present in the data, so unused factor levels no longer stack the panels in one column. Alluvial label sizes scale with the base font size of theme_use like the bar and heatmap labels (unchanged at the default size 14).

  • plt_alluvial() gains label_args$pct_accuracy, accepts label_args$style = "count_percent_wrap" (group name above count (percent)), and writes counts with a comma as thousands separator.

  • plt_dist(type = "bar") stacks the first fill category on top, in the order of the legend and of the alluvial strata (it was at the bottom).

  • plt_dist() converts labelled (haven_labelled) categories and facets with labelled::to_factor(), so plots, legends and named colours use the value labels instead of the numeric codes.

  • plt_dist(), plt_alluvial() and plt_sankey() share one internal helper for their list arguments, so a malformed list reports the plotting function (not merge_args()) as the source of the error, and plt_sankey() words a single unknown field in the singular.

UtilsR 0.6.8

  • New .cat_step() announces a numbered step ([i/n]) of a longer computation and marks it done with its elapsed time when the next step starts or the calling function returns. It wraps cli::cli_progress_step() and honours verbose.

  • .cat_message() gains style = "chip", which prints the timestamp in grey and colours only a short INFO / DONE / WARN / FAIL label, leaving the message text plain. The default style = "full" keeps the shaded line.

  • .cat_message() emits a cli message instead of cat() output, so suppressMessages() silences it (as it does set_wd()’s notice). It still prints to standard output in interactive sessions and shows braces as typed.

  • .cat_line(), .cat_box() and .cat_message() print type = "warning" labels in black on the yellow background; white text had too little contrast there.

  • plt_dist(type = "alluvial") removes categorical missing values before matching named colours, following the plt_alluvial() missing-row rule.

  • plt_alluvial() counts only observed facet/category combinations while preserving zero-count groups, avoiding the full cross-facet frequency table.

  • The lv() variable summary tints rows by variable type: character, numeric or integer, and factor (including ordered) variables.

  • plt_alluvial() retains only required input columns in its plot environment, keeping unused data out of serialized plot objects.

  • plt_alluvial() rejects out-of-range facet and legend dimensions with a clear argument error before integer conversion.

  • plt_alluvial() matches named colours to observed group names, ignoring unused names and rejecting incomplete or ambiguous named palettes.

  • plt_alluvial() removes and reports rows with explicit NA factor levels or SPSS user-defined missing values in its required columns.

  • plt_dist() treats plain numeric distribution and facet variables as categories in numeric ascending order in every plot mode. Existing factor orders, character ordering, named colours and missing-row rules are retained.

  • plt_alluvial() calculates labels with the final stratum layout, so labels follow later axis changes. It no longer builds the plot in advance for labels.

  • plt_alluvial() keeps real groups named .gap_1 or starting with .gap_ distinct from its transparent gap strata, including their labels.

  • When lv() finds no global data or data_all, its error names the data frames and Seurat objects in the global environment. Called without data, it reports that error directly again instead of as an unevaluable first argument.

  • The lv() variable-summary subtitle says it counts variables with missing or Unknown/Blank/N/A values, rather than reading as a count of values.

  • Seurat lv() cell statistics no longer list orig.ident, the sample identity, as a clustering.

  • lv() labels empty-string categories (blank) in its long count table and its default and grouped summaries, as its wide count table already did, unless a (blank) value exists and the two would merge.

  • Two-variable lv(count = ) tables skip the wide and row-percentage tables, with a message, when either variable has more than 100 categories; a 5,000-category wide table previously took about 18 seconds.

  • lv(group = ) rejects a grouping column with more than 100 distinct values or factor levels, pointing to count instead; a 5,000-value identifier used as the group previously took over a minute to tabulate.

  • lv() summarizes POSIXlt date-time columns in its frequency and grouped tables again instead of reporting them as list columns.

  • fct_cat()’s binary_ref is renamed ref_idx, in the same place: fct_cat(x, ref_idx = 1) or ref_idx = "No". binary_ref still works, with a deprecation warning, and giving both is an error.

  • lv() summarizes difftime columns as numbers in their own units and leaves list columns out of its frequency and grouped tables with a message; both previously made gtsummary fail.

  • count_packages_in_libpaths() counts installed packages instead of all library subdirectories, excluding installation locks and unrelated folders.

  • lv(count = ) warns that it ignores selections in ..., pattern and group, which it previously dropped silently.

  • Suggested lv() filters write numbers and logicals as literals when their text reads back exactly, and mark truncation with a trailing comment instead of a literal "..." value. Factor value counts and filters omit unused levels, matching the frequency-table labels.

  • Console lv() reports render the variable summary and frequency tables once, in their final group, instead of also rendering each beforehand; this saves about 40% of the printing time.

  • check_system() queries Windows memory, OS, and CPU information with PowerShell CIM, retaining WMIC as a fallback for older environments.

  • Grouped lv() summaries show missing group values as their own last group and include them in the overall column. They were previously dropped from both, while the reported group count still included them.

  • lv() inspects atomic vectors and matrices, returning them invisibly, instead of treating them as column selections of the global data, where lv(1:2) silently reported its first two columns. Bare column names and character vectors of column names still select from the default data, and an unevaluable first argument without default data reports its own error.

  • lv() leaves character and factor columns with more than 100 categories, such as identifiers, out of its frequency and grouped tables with a message; they stay in the variable summary. A 50,000-row identifier column previously took about four minutes to tabulate and now adds no table rows.

  • PlotHeatmapJaccard() excludes missing group labels and feature names from feature sets, preventing false overlaps, and reports missing groups clearly. Its default strip palette repeats beyond 16 groups instead of producing missing colours. Pairwise calculations reuse symmetry instead of computing both directions.

  • lv() highlights the category levels its special-value counts include, using the same whole-word rules, instead of separate substring matches that also coloured variable labels and missed markers such as “Not stated”.

  • fct_cat(binary_ref = ) also takes the reference levels by name: fct_cat(x, binary_ref = "No") keeps "No" and collapses the other levels to "Oth", as binary_ref = 2 does when "No" is the second level. An unknown name is an error. Integer indices work as before.

  • lv() summarizes entirely missing character columns in its default and grouped tables instead of failing in gtsummary formatting.

  • lv() summarizes date and date-time columns with more than ten distinct values instead of failing while truncating their suggested filter.

  • PlotRankCor() keeps missing scores out of ranks and correlations, both in its default rank mode and when applying a rank transform to raw scores. Min-max and z-score scaling also retain missing values and handle sparse groups without failing or manufacturing complete observations.

  • stat_ci() formats character intervals with vectorized dynamic precision, retaining detected precision and warnings while avoiding per-row templates.

  • stat_ci() removes the minus sign from formatted zeros without changing other rounding or unparsed text. The mean/SD example now reflects its actual sprintf() rounding.

  • stat_ci() preserves the names of x in numeric CI, mean/SD, and character modes, including missing observations and empty named vectors.

  • stat_ci() leaves missing and whitespace-only strings unchanged without warning, including Unicode whitespace, while still reporting other text that cannot be parsed as an interval.

  • Numeric stat_ci() rows with missing components return genuine missing strings, including SPSS user-missing codes and entirely missing logical vectors, instead of embedding missing-value text or codes in the result.

  • stat_ci() warns when reformatting drops trailing annotations such as a P-value. Ignoring trailing stars and a terminal period remains supported.

  • stat_ci() returns character(0) for empty character input, matching its numeric modes and documented return type.

  • stat_ci() rejects matrices, arrays, and unsupported numeric storage such as integer64 and time spans, avoiding silently flattened or misread values.

  • stat_ci() validates scalar integer precision before coercion or formatting in every mode and reports precision that exceeds the formatted-number limit.

  • lv() retains empty cross-tabulation categories in wide tables, displaying them as (blank) and disambiguating an existing category with that label.

  • plt_dist() uses complete required rows in every mode and reports how many rows were removed. Unrelated missing columns are ignored; no usable rows produce an explicit error instead of an empty plot.

  • plt_dist() consistently validates distinct column selectors, facets, and transparency across plot modes. Three-variable heatmaps now truly ignore type, as documented.

  • plt_dist() shows a fill legend for unlabelled heatmaps and preserves custom visible legend positions; labelled tiles still hide the legend.

  • plt_dist() maps named colours to categories in every mode, checks category coverage, and keeps unnamed palette positions for unused factor levels in bars and heatmaps. Shared colour resolvers are unchanged.

  • Two-variable lv() cross-tabulations reuse one frequency table for the long counts, wide counts, and row percentages, retaining their output.

  • plt_dist() rejects heatmap cells with multiple fill categories instead of hiding categories under overlapping tiles. Heatmap examples use one category per cell; repeated observations of that category remain valid.

  • lv() constructs suggested filters as R expressions, correctly escaping non-syntactic column names, quotes, backslashes, and line breaks in values.

  • plt_dist() treats bar facet column names literally, including spaces, operators, and backticks, instead of parsing them as formula expressions.

  • plt_dist() ignores unrelated dplyr groups and rowwise grouping when counting categories, so input grouping cannot split bars or labels.

  • lv() emits native knitr tables with their dependencies in documented results = 'asis' chunks, avoiding duplicated report tables and console listings while knitting. The data-inspection vignette uses that format.

  • plt_dist() keeps bar counts, proportions, and labels separate from identically named input columns, preserving categories and plotted values.

  • lv() returns zero-row and zero-column inputs unchanged with a message, before report construction or temporary theme changes in every data-frame mode.

  • lv() supports renamed selections and keeps explicit empty selections empty, including selection of only the grouping column. Omitted selections still inspect all columns. Patterns are validated and warn when overriding unevaluated selections; input data and global-data shortcuts are preserved.

  • Seurat lv() uses the same column-name resolution as data frames, including character variables and group = TRUE, and forwards resolved controls without collisions with metadata column names.

  • lv() resolves bare group/count columns before caller objects, accepts character names from enclosing functions, and rejects invalid or repeated names instead of silently switching to an ungrouped summary.

  • lv() restores the complete existing gtsummary theme after successful reports and after errors, instead of clearing it or leaving Compact active.

  • lv() keeps cross-tabulation counts, percentages, and row totals separate from identically named input columns or categories, and counts only the requested variables when input carries dplyr grouping.

  • fct_to_combine() excludes missing rows from combination grouping and returns immediately when every row is missing, retaining missing-value and observed-level semantics. Complete inputs keep their existing grouping path.

  • fct_to_combine() documents group-wise factor-level merging in dplyr and shows how to retain a whole-data level order with the data-frame method.

  • fct_to_combine() rejects matrix/array selectors and raw vectors explicitly rather than passing them to column indexing or factor conversion.

  • fct_to_combine() recognizes an explicitly named data-frame x regardless of the order of named controls, while vector arguments retain their order.

  • fct_to_combine() rejects ambiguous output names, including a default name matching several existing columns, before replacing any column.

  • fct_to_combine() validates column-name shortcuts before selection and ignores names attached to selector vectors in both data-frame and data-mask calls, so duplicate columns cannot silently become a single input.

  • fct_to_combine() copies data.table inputs before writing results and invalidates keys and indices affected by replacement, preventing incorrect grouping after a key column is overwritten.

  • stat_pval() rejects impossible strict P-value bounds (<0 and >1), including scientific notation, while retaining inclusive bounds and plain number formatting. Decimal text is checked before floating-point rounding can turn a tiny positive endpoint into zero or an endpoint below one into one.

  • stat_pval() accepts Unicode whitespace around numeric text and after bound operators, including non-breaking and thin spaces copied from tables.

  • stat_pval() avoids formatting missing values and existing bound labels, while retaining a direct path for complete numeric vectors.

  • stat_ci_parse() shares significance-map validation with stat_pval(), including empty maps, empty symbols and duplicate thresholds; its default mapping continues to stop at * without a marginal-significance dot.

  • stat_pval() checks decimal precision against the formatter’s output limit and returns empty vectors before allocating display thresholds.

  • stat_pval() accepts entirely missing logical vectors in formatting and annotation paths, while continuing to reject observed logical values.

  • stat_pval() displays signed zero like ordinary zero in P-value modes, retaining its significance symbol and the existing plain-number display.

  • fct_to_combine() groups integer factor codes before sorting combinations and constructing labels, reducing repeated work when many rows share groups. Only observed combinations are retained, in the same factor-level order.

  • fct_to_combine() errors when distinct input combinations produce the same label, rather than silently merging groups. Repeated identical combinations remain valid.

  • fct_to_combine() propagates missing inputs to genuine missing results, including NaN and SPSS user-missing codes and ranges. The literal string "NA" remains a category. Class methods are registered for restored labelled and integer64 inputs before combining them.

  • fct_to_combine() validates vector dimensions, separators, selected column names and output names. Unused arguments to the data-frame method now error instead of silently ignoring misspelled controls.

  • fct_to_combine() ignores vector names when constructing labels and sorting levels, preventing columns such as collapse or na.last from changing the output length or level order in programmatic calls.

  • stat_pval() matches significance thresholds across the vector rather than calling a function for each P-value, retaining all existing star cutoffs.

  • stat_pval() preserves input names and returns character vectors for empty inputs in every mode. Matrix and array inputs now fail explicitly.

  • stat_pval() validates significance maps consistently in formatting and annotation paths. Empty maps disable stars; empty symbols and first-match precedence for tied thresholds are retained.

  • stat_pval() validates digits before integer conversion. Fractional, missing, nonfinite, non-scalar, and non-numeric values are rejected; zero decimal places are supported only in plain mode.

  • stat_pval() rejects integer64, date, date-time, and time-span storage before formatting values or adding stars; convert these inputs explicitly.

  • stat_pval() rejects nonfinite and out-of-range P-values in both formatting and annotation paths. Ordinary numbers in plain mode keep their range.

  • stat_pval() retains missing values after appending stars, including missing text supplied with add_star_p. Missing P-values leave observed annotation text unchanged.

  • stat_pval() preserves character P-value bounds without treating their endpoints as exact P-values or inferring significance stars. Malformed numeric strings now fail explicitly.

  • check_size() shades size cells on a log scale of bytes, so objects ten or a hundred times smaller than the largest keep a visible color instead of appearing white. Size bars remain linear.

  • check_size() warns when pattern overrides names or indices supplied in ..., matching check_na(). The ignored selection is still not evaluated.

  • check_size() colors a single object, or several equally sized objects, in the full red of the largest size instead of the palette midpoint.

  • check_size() gains method = "lobstr", which sizes objects with lobstr::obj_size(): rows include captured environments and compact ALTREP sizes, and the total counts storage shared between objects once. The default method = "object.size" keeps the previous estimates. lobstr is suggested.

  • check_size() gains envir, so objects in a function frame or any other environment can be inspected. It defaults to .GlobalEnv, keeping existing calls unchanged, and never searches parent environments.

  • check_size() switches to the next unit when a label would round up to 1024, showing 1.00 MB or 1.00 GB instead of 1024.00 KB or 1024.00 MB.

  • check_size() lists equally sized objects alphabetically for names and indices too, matching pattern and the default selection instead of following the order in which objects were supplied.

  • check_size() adds a source note stating that sizes are object.size() estimates, so the table itself warns that totals can double-count shared storage and that environments and closures may be underestimated.

  • check_size() renders its summary label as bold TOTAL instead of showing literal asterisks; the underlying data still label the row **TOTAL**.

  • check_size() warns when a top-level call passes an unquoted numeric variable, which is used as object indices rather than as the variable’s name.

  • check_size() includes each binding’s original error message in its combined read-failure warning without evaluating failed bindings again.

  • check_size() uses a neutral white size gradient for all-zero estimates, avoiding the misleading midpoint color of a zero-width domain.

  • check_size() sorts only names matched by pattern, avoiding a full global name sort while preserving alphabetical order among equally sized objects.

  • check_na() and lv() also count “Blanks”, “Unknowns”, “Not applicable”, “Not stated”, “Not reported”, “NULL” and values made only of ?, - or . as special values. The new check_na(special = ) argument replaces the built-in markers with user-supplied regular expressions, and special = character(0) turns special-value counting off.

  • check_na() returns its gt table visibly instead of printing it and returning the input data invisibly, so the table renders in R Markdown, Quarto and pkgdown and can be saved with gt::gtsave(). Calls that produce no table return NULL invisibly. Code that piped the returned data onward needs updating.

  • check_na() warns when pattern overrides a selection in ..., and reports an invalid pattern regular expression with a clear error.

  • check_na() adds a source note explaining its severity shading and documents the thresholds and the denominator of its summary percentages.

  • check_na() and lv() count special values about three to five times faster on columns with many distinct values, normalizing only values that contain whitespace and matching markers caselessly. A dotted capital I (U+0130) no longer folds to "i" when matching markers.

  • check_na() shades special-value cells from light to dark blue as their share rises, so the highest severity is no longer the palest.

  • The package description now names the exported check_na() function correctly.

  • check_na() displays small positive proportions as <0.1% in cells and <0.01% in summaries, distinguishing them from exact zeros.

  • check_na() and lv() skip unused factor levels when matching special-value markers, preserving counts and the original factor levels.

  • check_na() avoids integer overflow in dataset-size calculations and count formatting, including summaries with more than 2^31 - 1 data points or issues.

  • check_size() scales object bars to the largest individual estimate instead of the total, keeping large selections readable and capping the total bar.

  • check_na() and lv() load missing-value methods for serialized labelled and integer64 columns, preventing session-dependent errors or missed NA values.

  • check_size() skips global name enumeration for explicit character selectors, while retaining sorted numeric indices and pattern selection.

  • check_size() identifies its summary by row position, so an object named **TOTAL** retains the normal object styles and size gradient.

  • check_size() formats bars from raw sizes, respects later gt formatters, and keeps HTML bars out of LaTeX, RTF and Word output.

  • check_size() documents the limits of summed object-size estimates and the evaluation of active bindings and promises, with self-contained examples.

  • check_size() colors the visible size cells and uses consistent byte-to-GB labels in both the table and subtitle, keeping tiny objects distinct from zero.

  • check_size() reads each selected binding once, so size and class describe the same value even when an active binding changes between reads.

  • check_na() labels affected-variable counts explicitly in its subtitle, distinguishing them from the individual-value counts in the summary.

  • check_size() consistently returns a renderable gt table for empty selections, reports unreadable objects, and counts only successfully inspected objects.

  • check_na() validates pattern as NULL or one non-missing character string, with clear errors for invalid inputs. Empty patterns still match all columns.

  • check_size() validates object names, indices and regular expressions, deduplicates selections, and never expands unmatched selections or searches parent environments for missing objects.

  • check_size() renders its size bars directly in HTML, avoiding per-object plots and temporary SVG files while handling zero-sized objects.

  • check_na() rounds percentages only for display and uses unrounded values for severity colors, correcting double rounding and threshold misclassification.

  • check_na() and lv() preserve class-specific missing-value semantics when counting special values, so SPSS user-missing codes are not counted twice.

  • check_na() and lv() use Unicode-aware word boundaries and whitespace normalization, avoiding false matches within accented words and recognizing non-breaking spaces and other Unicode blanks.

  • check_na() constructs its summary in one operation, reducing overhead on wide datasets while preserving counts, ordering, formatting and table styles.

  • check_na() and lv() recognize whitespace-only blanks and markers with repeated spaces, tabs or newlines. Matching still runs on distinct values, counts each value once, and keeps actual NA values separate.

  • check_na() rejects ambiguous column names, multidimensional selected columns, and invalid show_all values with informative errors, preventing duplicated counts and missingness percentages above 100% for matrix columns.

  • check_na() returns empty inputs unchanged with an informational message, avoiding undefined percentages and empty-table errors.

  • check_na() supports renamed selections, inspects all columns by default for grouped inputs, and no longer expands unmatched selections or patterns to the full dataset. Explicit selections inspect the chosen columns across all rows.

  • check_na() preserves the complete input and its attributes when inspecting selected columns, including calls where the selected columns have no issues.

  • fct_num() documents and demonstrates reduced bin counts after quantile ties, merged factor levels from repeated labels, and the handling of infinite data in fixed-cut and automatic binning modes. These behaviors are unchanged.

  • fct_num(type = "equal") computes plain numeric ranges without concatenating or filtering the full vector, reducing allocations while retaining cut points, missing values, and class-specific range methods.

  • fct_num() rejects time-span objects supplied as nbins, preventing their conversion to seconds from silently requesting a different number of bins. Valid numeric and integer64 bin counts retain their existing behavior.

  • fct_num() documents that automatic fixed-cut labels follow numeric formatting options such as scipen, and shows explicit labels for stable factor levels.

  • fct_num() constructs fixed-cut interval labels in one vectorized operation, reducing overhead when many cut points are supplied while preserving labels and interval order.

  • fct_num() avoids full-vector missing-value masks and redundant filtering for ordinary complete numeric data, and skips unused quantile names. Classed-vector dispatch, missing values, and group boundaries are preserved.

  • fct_num(type = "equal") reports when numeric precision produces repeated cut points, with guidance to reduce the bin count or supply explicit cut points. It does not merge bins or move their boundaries.

  • fct_num() rejects logical labels before computing cut points, so labels = FALSE cannot return integer codes when quantile ties leave one group.

  • fct_num() rejects matrices and arrays instead of silently flattening multidimensional data into a factor vector.

  • fct_num() rejects Duration, Period, and Interval data and cut points before using their numeric storage. Convert them to explicitly chosen numeric units first to avoid incorrect ranges or ignored time components.

  • fct_num() rejects SPSS user-missing data and cut points with a message to normalize them first, preventing missing codes from entering valid groups or influencing automatic cut points.

  • fct_num() reuses integer bin codes for ordinary numeric data and unique text labels, reducing factor-construction allocations. Classed inputs and nonstandard labels retain the existing cut() path and group semantics.

  • fct_num() reports constant data explicitly in both automatic binning modes, without misleading zero-bin warnings or label-length errors. Fixed-cut behavior and right-closed group boundaries are unchanged.

  • fct_num() validates nbins before conversion, rejecting fractional, missing, non-scalar, non-numeric, or overflowing counts without coercion warnings or silently changing the requested number of bins.

  • fct_num() increases automatic label precision only when cut-point text collides, preventing nearby numeric intervals from merging into one level.

  • fct_num() validates fixed cut points before sorting, rejecting missing, non-finite, duplicate, or non-numeric values instead of silently changing groups or assigning misleading labels.

  • fct_num() rejects unsupported integer64 data and cut points instead of silently misclassifying their values or losing missing observations.

  • fct_cat() reuses matched level positions when recoding and keeps unmatched levels in a vector, avoiding an intermediate list and repeated membership tables for factors with many levels.

  • fct_cat(new_labels = ...) returns the original factor when normalized, non-missing labels are unchanged, avoiding an unnecessary observation copy.

  • fct_cat() clears obsolete stats::reorder() scores after changing levels or recode mappings. Operations that leave both unchanged retain the scores and other metadata.

  • fct_cat() rejects reorder calls that mix character levels and numeric positions. Numeric arguments are normalized separately before combining, including calls that mix native numbers and classed numeric indices.

  • fct_to_group() delegates index checks to fct_cat(), avoiding a warning for empty groups and an unrelated if error for missing indices.

  • fct_cat(binary_ref = ...) requires at least one reference index instead of silently putting every observed level into "Oth" for an empty input.

  • fct_cat() validates replacement labels after character conversion. Classed character labels can no longer bypass merging or missing-label removal, and conversions that change the label count are rejected.

  • fct_cat() ignores names attached to a reorder vector. A named vector that leaves the level order unchanged preserves the original contrasts and model-matrix encoding.

  • fct_cat() normalizes numeric indices after validating their values and bounds. Classed indices such as bit64::integer64 now select the intended levels in recoding, grouping, reordering and binary conversion.

  • fct_cat() returns the original factor when reordering leaves its levels unchanged, avoiding a full-length allocation for an unchanged order, empty factors and one-level reversals.

  • fct_cat() checks old recode levels in one batch instead of rebuilding a membership table for every group, reducing time and allocation when there are many levels and groups.

  • fct_cat() determines used output groups from the original level counts and constructs recoded observations once, combining regrouping and unused-level removal without an intermediate full-length factor.

  • fct_cat() indexes level maps with factor codes directly, removing an extra full-length integer copy during reordering and unused-level removal.

  • fct_cat(new_labels = ...) and fct_label() reject lists and other non-atomic label containers instead of interpreting them as grouping instructions. Atomic numeric labels remain supported.

  • fct_cat() clears matrix-valued contrasts when the output levels change, preventing stale contrast rows and redundant model-matrix columns after regrouping. Names, labels and contrast function names remain preserved.

  • fct_cat() remaps integer factor codes when changing level order or dropping unused levels, avoiding character conversion and rebuilding. Unique, non-missing replacement labels use a direct levels update; duplicate and missing labels retain their existing merging semantics.

  • fct_cat() preserves factor names, class and metadata such as label across recoding and reordering. An explicit NA level remains distinct from missing codes; recoding still removes unused levels.

  • fct_cat() validates scalar logical flags, finite integer indices, non-empty group names, duplicate reorder levels and unknown recode levels. Recode groups can mix index-based and label-based specifications; each group is resolved before checking for overlapping old levels.

  • fct_cat() includes non-empty ... in its mode exclusivity check, instead of silently ignoring recode or reorder arguments when another mode is active.

  • fct_cat(binary_ref = ...) rejects a reference label of "Oth" when other levels remain, instead of silently merging both binary groups.

  • fct_cat() and fct_to_group() correctly merge into an existing, unmatched level; that level’s name no longer overwrites the mapping and turns the recoded observations into missing values.

  • plt_cat(), plt_con(), plt_dist(), plt_na() and plt_upset() gain save, and plt_alluvial() and plt_sankey() stop saving at RegR::save_plt()’s generic 10 x 11 in: a save list that leaves out width or height writes the page the plot is laid out for, with room for its levels, variables or panels beside the measured axis text and legends. Every call prints that size with a pasteable save line and the plot carries it as attr(p, "plot_size"); a supplied dimension is kept. The size and the saving need RegR 0.1.3 or later. plt_upset(output = "all") saves the combined plot and output = "data" refuses a save; plt_con(combine = FALSE) refuses one too. A split.by figure of plt_cat() or plt_con() is reported once, not per panel.

  • fmt_axisTile(mode = "tile") returns a ggplot for a ggplot, and a list of ggplots for a list of them; it wrapped each one in a patchwork, which drew the same color strip but changed the object’s class.

  • fmt_axisTile()’s text_size, text_face, text_angle and text_color default to NULL, which keeps the plot’s own axis text style. They were 9, "plain", 45 degrees on the x axis and "black", so even mode = "text", meant only to color the labels, made them smaller, black and rotated. Pass text_angle = 45 for the earlier rotated labels.

  • fmt_raster()’s default "ggrastr" backend draws each raster after an empty opaque polygon, as the "ragg" and "image" backends do: pdf() painted points drawn after a translucent grob, such as text with alpha = 0.3, with that transparency. A repeated call rasterizes a layer once, at the latest dpi.

  • fmt_plot_base() applies scale_y_list and scale_x_list with fmt_scale(). Each panel keeps its scale type, so a discrete or date axis no longer fails with “Discrete value supplied to a continuous scale”, and an existing scale keeps the settings the list does not name: a scale_y_log10() used to turn linear, with a “Scale for y is already present” message for every panel.

  • fmt_plot() no longer has an unused ...: a misspelled or unsupported argument, such as fmt_strip_list, is an “unused argument” error instead of being ignored without notice.

  • fmt_expand() warns when a plot’s coordinate system has expand = FALSE, which makes ggplot2 ignore the scale expansion it sets.

  • fmt_tag() labels use the font family of each plot’s theme (its plot.tag element), as patchwork tags do. Outside labels always used the device font, and inside labels did too with ggpp before 0.6.0 (Windows R has 0.5.8.1), so a theme_bw(base_family = "serif") figure got sans-serif tags. A family passed in ... still wins for inside labels.

  • fmt_legend() keeps a legend.justification or legend.justification.inside passed through ...; the justification derived from legend.position replaced it (causalR’s balance plot set it again after the call).

  • fmt_legend(legend.position = c(x, y)) centres the legend on a coordinate of exactly 0.5: c(0.5, 0.95) put the legend’s left edge on the panel’s centre line, so a “top centre” legend sat right of centre. Other coordinates and the corner codes keep their justification.

  • fmt_text() sets a patchwork’s axis_titles only when xlab or ylab is supplied. Changing only a title, a caption or text styles merged the axis titles too and replaced an existing "keep". A misspelt axis_titles is still rejected.

  • An empty string now removes a title without leaving space, as documented: fmt_text(title = "", xlab = "", ...) (also ylab, subtitle and caption) kept an empty title row of about 6 mm and an empty axis title row of about 5 mm, and fmt_legend(title = "") kept about 5.6 mm above the keys.

  • fmt_text(axis_title_size, axis_title_face, axis_title_color) also reach axis title sides that set the same field themselves. A theme with an explicit axis.title.x size, as several RegR plots use, kept that size and ignored the requested one. Blank sides stay blank.

  • fmt_plot() and fmt_plot_base() format each plot of a plain list and return the list. A list gave NULL, because patchwork’s & falls back to + for anything but a patchwork; a list holding a non-plot is an error.

  • fmt_axis() warns when plot_dims differs from the layout of a patchwork without nested patchworks. Such a patchwork’s own layout decides which axes are hidden, so plot_dims = c(4, 1) on a 2 x 2 grid was silently treated as c(2, 2). The help also points to patchwork::plot_layout(axes = "collect"), which removes only identical axes.

  • fmt_text() styles rich text elements in place: a title or axis title set with ggtext::element_markdown() in the plot or global theme keeps its class and settings, where styling it failed with “Only elements of the same class can be merged”.

  • fmt_text(legend_title = ) titles legends as fmt_legend(title = ) does. A continuous colour bar stays a colour bar instead of becoming a key legend, guide settings such as ncol and reverse are kept, linewidth legends are titled too, a vector sets one title per plot instead of failing, and ggplot2 4.0 no longer reports unknown labels or duplicated aesthetics.

  • fmt_text() formats the data plots of nested patchworks and skips spacers, guide areas and inset overlays, as the other formatters do. Per-plot labels no longer land on a spacer or the wrong plot, the first plot of a nested layout is no longer left out, and a title added after an outside fmt_tag() label is drawn once instead of twice (or not at all in a list).

  • The help pages of fmt_plot() and fmt_plot_base() show links and code formatting instead of raw Markdown such as [fmt_axis()] and **every**.

  • fmt_axisTile() warns once, when the plot is drawn, if no name in colors matches the axis values; a misspelled or wrongly cased name gave grey tiles or plain labels without notice. Axes with free facet scales are not checked.

  • fmt_scale() gives an updated scale its own copy of the secondary axis. The copy shared the input plot’s axis, and ggplot2 fills a dup_axis()’s derived breaks and labels when a plot is drawn: drawing the result gave the input plot’s secondary axis the result’s breaks.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ggrastr"), the default, rasterizes only point and tile layers, as ggrastr::rasterise() does by default. Lines, bars and polygons stay vector: as images they made a PDF larger (a 6-facet scatter with a smooth and a reference line: 103 KB, now 31 KB; 13 KB as vectors). A plot without such layers no longer warns about disabled clipping.

  • fmt_strip() no longer keeps its call frame in the plots it returns. Each call on a faceted plot stored further copies of the input plots and their data: a 21 MB plot relabelled three times serialized to 90 MB, now 22 MB. fmt_strip2() did the same for panels holding a native single-panel facet.

  • fmt_panel() keeps displayed grids visible. Without grid_color, a grid drawn in the panel background colour, such as theme_gray()’s white grid with bg = "white", becomes "grey70"; before, only restored grids were checked. Grids restored under a blank root line (theme_void()) are "grey85" instead of the root line’s black.

  • fmt_strip() with label = NULL keeps the labels of a faceted plot and changes only the strip style. It renamed every panel Figure1, so fmt_strip(p, label_fill = "steelblue") lost the facet levels. Unfaceted plots are still labelled Figure1, Figure2, etc.

  • fmt_strip() matches named labels of a faceted plot to its facet levels: c("8" = "Eight", "4" = "Four") labelled the 4-cylinder panel “Eight”. Unnamed levels keep their label. Unnamed labels whose number is neither one nor the number of levels, and names matching no level, now give a warning instead of being recycled or dropped silently.

  • fmt_strip() with label_fill keeps the theme’s strip border on faceted plots, as it already did on unfaceted ones; it drew a black border, so one figure could mix framed and unframed strips. On themes without a strip background, such as theme_minimal(), neither draws a border.

  • fmt_strip2()’s label_color defaults to "auto": each header uses black or white text, whichever contrasts more with its fill. Black bold text on the darkest generated grey ("#636363", used with one column or three or more) had a contrast of 3.5:1; it is now white. Pass label_color = "black" for the earlier text.

  • fmt_panel(grid = "keep") leaves the grid lines as they are, so the border or background can be changed alone; any other call removed or reset the grid, as the default grid = "none" still does.

  • fmt_flatten() given axes without axis_titles drops the input’s axis_titles as well, so axis titles follow axes as in wrap_plots() instead of staying collected.

  • fmt_flatten() errors name fmt_flatten() (or flatten_patchwork()) rather than an internal helper and report the class of an unsupported element, without descending into list-based objects such as data frames or gt tables.

  • fmt_flatten() is the new name of flatten_patchwork(), so it is found with the other fmt_* formatters. flatten_patchwork() remains as the same function without a deprecation warning.

  • fmt_raster(method = "image") takes any figure that draws itself: grobs, recorded base plots (replayed) and classed objects with a print method, such as RegR::plt_eff2()’s forestplot, which it rejected as a list of non-ggplot objects. Only a plain list holds several plots.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") and method = "image" leave the random stream where it was: ragg before 1.5.1 drew from it to name each capture device, so a later random step gave other results than without the raster.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") and method = "image" rasters are drawn opaque by pdf(), which painted a raster with the transparency of the translucent grob drawn before it.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") keeps the panel’s background grid and border vector and drops empty grobs, so they no longer add whole-panel images; a 200,000-point facetted plot written with pdf() is about 40% smaller.

  • fmt_raster(method = "image") has no plot margins, so at its own size the image is drawn pixel for pixel instead of shrunk to about 95%.

  • fmt_boxplot() releases temporary construction bindings after native layer creation, avoiding an extra serialized data copy while retaining deferred callbacks, formulas, position objects and symbolic constructor calls.

  • fmt_boxplot() combines source mappings with explicit fixed summary arguments when resolving independent identity overlays, including partial summaries and horizontal boxplots.

  • fmt_boxplot() retains precomputed outlier mappings for independent identity overlays when outlier shape is explicit, including an explicit NULL. Default suppression and explicit outliers = FALSE remain unchanged.

  • fmt_boxplot() snapshots inherited position settings as well as local settings, so edits to a supplied position or its parent do not alter overlays.

  • fmt_boxplot() retains raw source positions when staged mappings are nested inside arithmetic or function calls, preserving their environments and axes.

  • fmt_boxplot() constructs returned layers in an isolated environment and stores symbolic argument calls, avoiding retention of the source-resolution workspace and duplicate data in layer constructor calls.

  • fmt_boxplot() copies explicit position objects and their settings per plot leaf, preventing variable-width adjustment and later edits from changing the caller’s position, existing layers or sibling overlays.

  • fmt_boxplot() retains source notch boundaries and relative width mappings for independent identity-statistic overlays when those features are requested, including horizontal summaries and layer-level overrides.

  • fmt_boxplot() accepts anonymous and environment-selected function calls in automatic position mappings without failing during evaluation-stage lookup.

  • fmt_boxplot() formats plot leaves in one traversal and skips source lookup when independent data and complete mappings are explicit, preserving deferred callbacks, nested layouts and input validation.

  • fmt_boxplot() resolves complete vertical or horizontal summary mappings automatically for independent identity-statistic overlays, retaining source groups and deferred data callbacks while leaving explicit mappings unchanged.

  • fmt_boxplot() retains explicit NULL controls, including width and alpha, instead of replacing them with wrapper defaults. Omitted controls retain their existing defaults and explicit values follow native validation.

  • fmt_boxplot() copies raw positions from staged source mappings while omitting computed-statistic and after-scale positions in independent overlays. Explicit boxplot mappings keep their evaluation stages and environments.

  • fmt_point() skips unused factor strata during sampling, avoiding empty per-group work and matrix-column subsets while retaining data factor levels, missing groups, sampling order and column attributes.

  • fmt_point() normalizes pch and point/jitter cex aliases before applying omitted defaults. Explicit shape/size arguments retain priority, and beeswarm cex keeps its existing layout meaning and argument-list precedence.

  • fmt_point() snapshots supplied position objects and inherited settings per plot leaf, isolating edits to sibling overlays and caller-owned positions.

  • fmt_point() samples mappings with anonymous or dynamically selected functions without failing when the call has no static function name.

  • fmt_point() accepts external factor levels and labels during sampling, including positional configuration arguments and ordered factors. External row vectors in the factor input still require columns in layer data.

  • fmt_point() constructs point, beeswarm and rasterized layers in isolated environments, so extracted plot leaves do not retain unrelated input plots. Layer constructor calls keep symbolic arguments instead of embedding data.

  • fmt_point() retains missing character shapes during white-border normalization instead of failing before ggplot2 handles missing points.

  • fmt_point() samples indices before slicing matrix-column data, avoiding full-data group copies while retaining native binding and matrix attributes.

  • fmt_point() samples joint discrete colour/fill strata and existing facets; explicit groups retain priority, and layers missing facet columns still replicate.

  • fmt_point() respects explicit point/jitter positions supplied through ..., including position objects and native position names.

  • fmt_point() diagnoses fixed aesthetic vectors and external row-vector mappings before sampling, with instructions to map columns in layer data.

  • fmt_point() uses exact parameter lookups, preventing ignored geom arguments from partially matching inheritance, shape, colour or fill controls.

  • fmt_point() resolves dodge groups from built layer data, so continuous or NULL aesthetics retain plain jitter widths and data callbacks remain deferred.

  • fmt_point() supports group-only jitter-dodge on ggplot2 3.5.x without adding visible aesthetics or changing ggplot2 4.x positioning.

  • fmt_point() samples rows independently of hidden dplyr grouping attributes; rowwise and grouped inputs follow the same aesthetic-based sample limits.

  • fmt_point() distinguishes ordinary columns named stage, after_stat, after_scale or from_theme from delayed aesthetic function calls.

  • fmt_point(white_border = TRUE) keeps non-fillable symbols visible using a white underlay, and handles named shapes and an explicit NULL shape.

  • fmt_point() uses the raw start expression of staged aesthetics for stratified sampling while retaining later colour transformations.

  • fmt_point() samples row indices before slicing grouped data, reducing copying while preserving row order and random selections. Matrix columns retain the existing path; single-column data frames keep their dimensions.

  • fmt_point() validates sample sizes, seeds and layout controls consistently, rejects malformed jitter options and incompatible grouping lengths, and accepts NULL jitter dimensions for ggplot2’s native defaults.

  • fmt_point() forwards supported beeswarm.args options such as priority and side, and rejects unknown, duplicate or unnamed options.

  • fmt_point() includes explicit and layer-local groups in automatic dodging and ignores parent mappings when inherit.aes = FALSE.

  • fmt_point() respects layer-local mappings and inherit.aes when sampling and styling points. Explicit shape/size values override mappings, while omitted values retain the mapped aesthetics.

  • fmt_point() supports sampling function/formula data after the callback runs at build time. Sampling callbacks do not capture unrelated plots or data.

  • fmt_point(white_border = TRUE) retains scaled group colours and existing fills, treats color and colour consistently, and supports mapped shapes and shape 25 without replacing the original plot’s scales.

  • fmt_point() adds independent point layers to every nested patchwork leaf while preserving layout, annotations, spacers and the original plots.

  • fmt_point() samples expression-based groups, retains missing groups, and prioritizes explicit groups over discrete colour/fill mappings. Continuous colour/fill values no longer create one sampling group per distinct value.

  • fmt_point() preserves the caller’s random-number state when sampling, including calls that keep all rows and sessions without an existing seed.

  • check_na() and lv() count a special value (“unknown”, “blank”, “n/a”, “na”, “missing”, “unspecified”, “not available” or an empty string) only as a whole word and once per value. “Regional”, “Canada”, “anaplastic” or “NACT” no longer count through “na”, and “Unknown/unstaged/unspecified” counts once instead of twice. Matching runs on the distinct values, which makes check_na() about ten times and lv() about a third faster on a 257,000-row SEER table.

  • fmt_ref() keeps batching with scalar na.rm and lineend arguments while retaining native rendering, missing-value warnings and fallback for other args.

  • fmt_ref() creates separate reference layers for each subplot, so subsequent edits to one subplot’s reference data or styles do not alter its peers.

  • fmt_ref() uses native per-line layers when facet expressions reference its helper-column prefix, preserving panels without evaluating data callbacks.

  • fmt_ref() constructs self-contained reference mappings and layers, avoiding retention of peer plots and their data when a formatted subplot is extracted.

  • fmt_ref() uses factor color labels consistently in batched and native layers, preserving numeric palette indices, missing colors and encoded transparency.

  • Dedicated fmt_ref() regression tests cover native rendering, transformed and non-numeric positions, nested containers, input preservation and deferred data.

  • fmt_ref() gives argument-specific errors for empty and non-vector line styles when positions are supplied. Unused styles, native missing-value semantics, date positions and discrete category labels are retained.

  • fmt_ref() rejects colour with a suggestion to use its color parameter, avoiding duplicate aesthetics and silently ignored colour requests.

  • fmt_ref() batches reference lines by direction, retaining per-line styles, facet replication and existing colour scales. Other geom arguments keep the native per-line path for compatibility.

  • fmt_ref() rejects geom intercept argument names with a clear suggestion to use x and y. The formatting vignette now uses those supported arguments.

  • fmt_boxplot() aligns independent overlays with scalar fixed source x or y positions by mapping those constants before computing statistics. Explicit boxplot positions and cleared mappings retain priority; fixed vectors are not copied and data callbacks remain deferred.

  • fmt_boxplot() tries range-only blank layers after ordinary sample layers, retaining blank-only sources and documenting explicit source selection when point annotations share a plot with sample points.

  • fmt_boxplot() supports independent vector mappings without an explicit data frame while retaining their environments and deferred evaluation.

  • fmt_boxplot() retains the first single-axis source instead of replacing it with later two-axis layers in independent overlays.

  • fmt_boxplot() preserves the mapping-source order when explicit data are supplied, avoiding unused parent columns in independent overlays.

  • fmt_boxplot() matches data, mapping and stat argument names exactly, preventing unrecognized names from changing samples or statistics while retaining native geom validation and warnings.

  • fmt_boxplot() preserves explicit summary mappings for identity statistics, supporting vertical and horizontal precomputed boxplots without injecting unrelated raw-data axes. Data callbacks remain deferred.

  • fmt_boxplot() selects data and position mappings actually used by existing layers before unused parent settings, avoiding incompatible or empty parent samples. Automatic empty data frames are skipped; explicit empty data and deferred callbacks retain their normal behaviour.

  • fmt_boxplot() skips text, label, segment, curve and reference-line layers when selecting samples automatically, preserving valid single-axis sources instead of replacing them with annotation coordinates.

  • fmt_boxplot() preserves explicitly cleared x or y mappings in independent overlays, including cleared mappings inherited from an existing source layer.

  • fmt_boxplot() rejects malformed argument lists, invalid inheritance flags, non-aesthetic mappings and non-plot gg components with clear input errors.

  • fmt_boxplot() honours explicitly supplied outlier shapes, including NULL, while retaining hidden outlier markers as the default.

  • fmt_boxplot() formats every leaf of nested patchworks while preserving layouts, annotations, plot-list names and non-plot placeholders or overlays.

  • fmt_boxplot() resolves independent overlays from existing layer data and position mappings, preserving deferred evaluation and single-axis boxplots. Missing sources now give a clear error instead of enabling inheritance.

  • fmt_boxplot() retains explicit data, mappings and deferred data callbacks in independent layers, filling only missing position mappings from the plot.

  • fmt_panel() lets restored grid placeholders inherit blank parent-grid settings during and after formatting, preserving explicit blank-inheritance overrides and the restoration of grids hidden by a blank root line.

  • fmt_panel() gives automatically restored grids contrasting colours when a blank root line hides them, including on dark panels with theme_void(), while preserving explicit colours and transparent backgrounds.

  • fmt_panel() retains empty themes in its batch cache on older ggplot2 versions, keeping batch grid output identical to formatting plots individually.

  • fmt_panel() reuses a recent additional theme in batches, including after the four-theme cache stops scanning, avoiding repeated grid resolution when later plots share a theme.

  • fmt_panel() checks automatically restored grid contrast against the colour of transparent panel fills composited over a known opaque plot background, preserving background transparency and explicit grid colours.

  • fmt_panel() rejects themes, aesthetic mappings and other non-plot gg components instead of returning a theme or silently producing NULL.

  • fmt_panel() corrects matching background colours in automatically restored major, minor and axis-specific grids while preserving explicit plot styles.

  • fmt_his() follows binned position mappings before and after statistics, matching native distribution counts and geometry while preserving original points, axes and unscaled mappings.

  • fmt_his() delegates unscaled distributions without an x scale to native ggplot2 statistics, retaining supported histograms instead of returning empty layers.

  • fmt_his() preserves final after_scale() x mappings without evaluating them again, keeping distribution positions aligned with native layers.

  • fmt_his() normalizes time-difference samples to numeric positions while retaining their units, preventing empty histogram and density overlays.
